newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares scrape to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares scrape to new record close.

text.p: Dutch shares scraped to another record close on Tuesday, helped by a firm opening on Wall Street, which perked up a languid Amsterdam bourse and sparked a late session rally.
The AEX index of leading stocks pushed to close at 830.77 points, a new record finish and up 1.44 points on the day. The intra-day peak at 832.45 was however below Monday's 834.43.
The mid-cap AMX index lost 13.18 points to 1,269.51.
"We've just followed the U.S. higher, there's no volume behind it," one dealer commented. "The market has settled into a range in the high 820s and is happy to trade there," he added.

Individual stocks ended mixed, with financials which led the way higher initially, coming off a little towards the close. Banks ABN AMRO and ING ended 0.20 higher and 0.10 guilders lower at 37.10 and 90.00 guilders respectively.
Elsewhere, retailer Ahold continued to attract some buying ahead of its first quarter results on Thursday.
Analysts expect the group which will incorporate its huge acquisition Stop&Shop in the United States, to post a hefty 75 percent rise in net profits on the same period last year.
Ahold shares gained 2.00 guilders to end at 155.00.
"Technically the share looks good and fundamentally the company looks good -- there's no real problem with that share," one dealer said.

But dealers noted the market would struggle to get beyond 834 points -- the recent peak -- where chartists have pegged the first technical resistance. A period of sideways trading was the most likely scenario near-term, they said.
